---
pagetitle: "crbcc: R bytecode compiler written in C"
output:
  html_document:
    theme: null
    highlight: null
    mathjax: null
params:
  ## The --csv reports of crbcc_bench.py. install has the suite install, from
  ## the image build. compile has the suites check and compile, from the CI.
  install: "install.csv"
  compile: "compile.csv"
  ## If this value is not empty, the report writes two files for the crbcc
  ## README to this directory: the figure install-time-top15.png and the
  ## shields.io badge speedup.json.
  assets: ""
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      dev = "png", dpi = 100, fig.width = 5.6)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(reactable)
library(htmltools)

## The categorical slots 1-2 of the dataviz reference palette, in a fixed order.
## The CSS of the page gets the same values.
COL    <- c(gnur = "#2a78d6", crbcc = "#eb6834")
NAME   <- c(gnur = "GNU R", crbcc = "crbcc")
INK    <- "#0b0b0b"  # primary text
INK2   <- "#52514e"  # secondary text, axes
INK3   <- "#898781"  # muted marks
GRID   <- "#e4e3df"  # grid lines
## The parts of the install time, from other slots of the same palette.
PART   <- c(native = "#9085e9", bytecode = "#eda100", rest = "#e87ba4")
COMPILERS <- names(COL)

## This list is the same as in crbcc_bench.py.
RECOMMENDED <- c("MASS", "lattice", "Matrix", "nlme", "survival", "boot",
                 "class", "cluster", "codetools", "foreign", "KernSmooth",
                 "mgcv", "nnet", "rpart", "spatial")

fmt   <- function(x, digits = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
pct   <- function(x) paste0(fmt(100 * x, 0), "%")
times <- function(x, digits = 1) paste0(fmt(x, digits), "x")
gmean <- function(x) { x <- x[is.finite(x) & x > 0]; exp(mean(log(x))) }
pkg_group <- function(package) if_else(package %in% RECOMMENDED, "recommended", "CRAN")
## A Markdown link to a crbcc commit on GitHub, with the short hash as text.
commit_link <- function(commit) {
  if (!grepl("^[0-9a-f]{40}$", commit)) return(sprintf("`%s`", commit))
  sprintf("[`%s`](https://github.com/PRL-PRG/crbcc/commit/%s)", substr(commit, 1, 7), commit)
}
## The environment of a benchmark, from the header of its CSV file.
machine  <- function(m) sprintf("%s, %s logical CPUs, %s %s", m$cpu_model %||% "unknown CPU",
                                m$logical_cpus, m$system, m$machine)
software <- function(m) sprintf("R %s, crbcc %s, commit %s", sub("^R version ([^ ]+).*", "\\1", m$r_version),
                                m$crbcc_version, commit_link(m$crbcc_commit))
started  <- function(m) paste(sub("T", " ", substr(m$timestamp, 1, 16)), "UTC")

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 15) + theme(
  text = element_text(colour = INK2),
  axis.title = element_text(size = rel(0.85)),
  axis.text = element_text(colour = INK2),
  axis.text.y = element_text(colour = INK),
  legend.text = element_text(colour = INK),
  legend.position = "top", legend.location = "plot", legend.justification = "left",
  legend.title = element_blank(), legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
  panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = GRID, linewidth = 0.3),
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
  plot.margin = margin(6, 14, 6, 6)))
compiler_fill <- scale_fill_manual(values = COL, breaks = COMPILERS, labels = NAME)

# Read the CSV files -------------------------------------------------------

## Returns the "# key: value" header (meta) and the rows (data) of a CSV file.
read_bench <- function(file) {
  lines <- readLines(file)
  meta <- sub("^# ", "", grep("^#", lines, value = TRUE))
  data <- read.csv(text = grep("^#", lines, value = TRUE, invert = TRUE),
                   colClasses = "character")
  list(meta = as.list(setNames(sub("^[^:]*: ", "", meta), sub(": .*", "", meta))),
       data = mutate(data, run = as.integer(run), value = as.numeric(value)))
}
ins <- read_bench(params$install)
clo <- read_bench(params$compile)

## A run with a failure still has its rows. The statistics do not use them.
RUN <- c("suite", "benchmark", "compiler", "run")
failed_runs <- function(d) d |> filter(failure != "") |> distinct(across(all_of(RUN)), failure)
passed <- function(d) anti_join(d, failed_runs(d), by = RUN)
failed <- bind_rows(failed_runs(ins$data), failed_runs(clo$data))

# Install benchmark --------------------------------------------------------

## One row for each package, with the median of the runs for each metric and
## compiler, for example elapsed_gnur. Only the packages with results of the
## two compilers. The longest elapsed_gnur is first.
ins_pkgs <- unique(ins$data$benchmark)
ins_runs <- n_distinct(ins$data$run)
pk <- passed(ins$data) |>
  filter(suite == "install") |>
  group_by(package = benchmark, compiler, metric) |>
  summarise(value = median(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(metric, compiler), values_from = value) |>
  filter(!is.na(elapsed_gnur), !is.na(elapsed_crbcc)) |>
  mutate(group = pkg_group(package), .after = package) |>
  arrange(desc(elapsed_gnur))

## The totals of all packages and of each group. less is the part of the
## GNU R elapsed time that crbcc saves.
tot <- bind_rows(pk, mutate(pk, group = "all")) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(packages = n(), across(matches("_(gnur|crbcc)$"), sum)) |>
  mutate(rest_gnur = elapsed_gnur - native_gnur - bytecode_gnur,
         rest_crbcc = elapsed_crbcc - native_crbcc - bytecode_crbcc,
         less = 1 - elapsed_crbcc / elapsed_gnur)
less  <- setNames(tot$less, tot$group)
n_grp <- setNames(tot$packages, tot$group)
all_pk <- filter(tot, group == "all")

# Compile benchmark --------------------------------------------------------

chk <- filter(clo$data, suite == "check")
n_chk <- sum(chk$value[chk$metric == "closures"])
n_chk_pkg <- n_distinct(chk$benchmark)
chk_failed <- failed_runs(chk)
cl_passes <- n_distinct(clo$data$iteration[clo$data$suite == "compile" & clo$data$metric == "compile"])
n_cl_pkg <- n_distinct(clo$data$benchmark[clo$data$suite == "compile"])

## One row for each closure: the median compile time of each compiler, the
## size in AST nodes, and the size class (powers of 10). Only the closures
## with results of the two compilers.
cl <- passed(clo$data) |>
  filter(suite == "compile", metric == "compile") |>
  group_by(package = benchmark, closure, size = as.numeric(size), compiler) |>
  summarise(time = median(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = compiler, values_from = time)
n_missing <- sum(is.na(cl$gnur) | is.na(cl$crbcc))
cl <- cl |>
  filter(!is.na(gnur), !is.na(crbcc)) |>
  mutate(class = cut(size, c(1, 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4, Inf), right = FALSE))

## One row for each package: the median pass time of each compiler. The
## time of a pass (the column iteration) is the sum of the compile times of
## its closures. Only the packages with results of the two compilers.
cl_pk <- passed(clo$data) |>
  filter(suite == "compile", metric == "compile") |>
  group_by(package = benchmark, compiler, iteration) |>
  summarise(time = sum(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(package, compiler) |>
  summarise(time = median(time), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = compiler, values_from = time) |>
  filter(!is.na(gnur), !is.na(crbcc))
cmp <- c(gnur = sum(cl_pk$gnur), crbcc = sum(cl_pk$crbcc))
## The headline: the geometric mean of the closure speedups. It does not use
## a closure with a zero time, because its speedup is 0 or infinite.
speedup <- gmean(cl$gnur / cl$crbcc)
n_zero <- sum(cl$gnur == 0 | cl$crbcc == 0)

# Badge for the README -----------------------------------------------------

if (nzchar(params$assets)) {
  dir.create(params$assets, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  writeLines(sprintf('{"schemaVersion": 1, "label": "compile speedup", "message": "%s faster than GNU R", "color": "blue"}',
                     times(speedup)),
             file.path(params$assets, "speedup.json"))
}
```

```{css}
}

  max-width: 800px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 16px 64px;
  background: var(--page); color: var(--ink);
  font: 16px/1.55 system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;
}
h1, h2, h3 { line-height: 1.2; color: var(--ink); }

h2 { font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 650; letter-spacing: -0.015em; margin: 56px 0 16px; }
h3 { font-size: 1.0625rem; font-weight: 600; margin: 0 0 8px; }
p, ul, ol, dl { margin: 0 0 12px; }
ul, ol { padding-left: 1.25rem; }
li { margin: 2px 0; }
a { color: inherit; text-decoration-color: var(--ink-3); text-underline-offset: 2px; }
a:hover { text-decoration-color: var(--ink); }
code { font: 0.875em var(--mono); background: var(--code); padding: 1px 4px; border-radius: 4px; white-space: nowrap; }
img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }

.hero { padding: 48px 0 8px; }
.eyebrow { font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-3); margin: 0 0 8px; }
.lede { font-size: 1.0625rem; color: var(--ink-2); max-width: 64ch; }
.links { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; margin: 20px 0 0; }
.links a { padding: 6px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 999px; background: var(--card); font-size: 0.875rem; text-decoration: none; }
.links a:hover { border-color: var(--ink-3); }

.tiles { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr)); gap: 12px; margin: 32px 0 12px; }
.tile { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; padding: 18px 20px; background: var(--card); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 12px; text-decoration: none; }
.tile:hover { border-color: var(--ink-3); }
.tile-label { font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--ink-2); }
.tile-value { font-size: 2.5rem; font-weight: 650; letter-spacing: -0.03em; line-height: 1.05; color: var(--good); }
.tile-value small { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0; color: var(--ink-2); margin-left: 6px; }
.tile.bad .tile-value { color: var(--bad); }
.tile-context { font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--ink-2); }

.note { font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--ink-2); border-left: 3px solid var(--ink-3); padding: 2px 0 2px 12px; margin: 16px 0; }
.alert { background: #fdf1f0; border: 1px solid #efc6c3; border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px 20px; margin: 16px 0; }
.alert h3 { color: var(--bad); }
.alert table { font-size: 0.8125rem; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; }
.alert td:last-child { min-width: 16rem; }
.alert th, .alert td { text-align: left; vertical-align: top; padding: 4px 8px; border-top: 1px solid #efc6c3; }
.scroll { overflow-x: auto; }

.level3 { background: var(--card); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px; margin: 0 0 12px; }
.level3 > :last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }
.caption { font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--ink-2); }
.level3 img { margin: 8px auto 12px; }

dl { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 6.5rem 1fr; gap: 8px 16px; font-size: 0.9375rem; }

dd { margin: 0; }
@media (max-width: 560px) {
  dl { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 0; }
  dt { margin-top: 10px; }
  dt:first-child { margin-top: 0; }
  .level3 { padding: 16px 14px; }
}

.dot, .sw { display: inline-block; width: 9px; height: 9px; border-radius: 50%; margin-right: 6px; vertical-align: 0; }
.sw { border-radius: 2px; }
.gnur .dot, .rt-th.gnur .rt-text-content::before { background: var(--gnur); }
.crbcc .dot, .rt-th.crbcc .rt-text-content::before { background: var(--crbcc); }
.sw.native, .seg.native { background: var(--native); }
.sw.bytecode, .seg.bytecode { background: var(--bytecode); }
.sw.rest, .seg.rest { background: var(--rest); }

.bars { display: grid; gap: 14px; margin: 12px 0 14px; }
.bar-head { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: 4px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.bar { display: flex; gap: 2px; height: 28px; }
.seg { flex: 0 0 0; min-width: 3px; border-radius: 4px; display: flex; align-items: center; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.seg:not(:empty) { padding: 0 7px; }
.key { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 4px 18px; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: var(--ink-2); margin-bottom: 12px; }

.rt-th.gnur .rt-text-content::before, .rt-th.crbcc .rt-text-content::before { content: ""; display: inline-block; width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; margin-right: 5px; }
.files { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; margin: 0 0 16px; }
.files a { font: 0.875rem var(--mono); padding: 6px 12px; background: var(--card); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; text-decoration: none; }
.files a:hover { border-color: var(--ink-3); }
/* macOS hides a default scrollbar. A styled scrollbar stays visible, thus
   the reader sees that the table has more rows. */
.rt-table::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 8px; height: 8px; }
.rt-table::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: var(--ink-3); border-radius: 4px; }
.rows { margin-top: 8px; }
```

<header class="hero">
<p class="eyebrow">crbcc benchmark report</p>
<h1>R bytecode compiler written in C</h1>
<p class="lede">crbcc gives the same byte code as the GNU R <code>compiler</code> package. It is faster, because it is written in C, not in R. It follows the same structure as the original compiler so all credit goes to Luke Tierney.</p>
<p class="links"><a href="https://github.com/PRL-PRG/crbcc#readme">README and source code</a><a href="https://prl-prg.github.io/crbcc/crbcc.html">Use crbcc</a><a href="https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=crbcc">crbcc on CRAN</a></p>
</header>

```{r tiles}
tile <- function(href, label, value, unit, context, class = "")
  tags$a(class = paste("tile", class), href = href, span(class = "tile-label", label),
         span(class = "tile-value", value, tags$small(unit)), span(class = "tile-context", context))
div(class = "tiles",
  tile("#install-results", "Install time", pct(less[["all"]]), "less",
       sprintf("R CMD INSTALL of %d packages: %s s with crbcc, %s s with GNU R.",
               n_grp[["all"]], fmt(all_pk$elapsed_crbcc), fmt(all_pk$elapsed_gnur))),
  tile("#compile-results", "Compile speedup", times(speedup), "faster",
       sprintf("Geometric mean of %s closure speedups, %d packages.", fmt(nrow(cl), 0), n_distinct(cl$package))),
  if (nrow(chk_failed) == 0)
    tile("#check-method", "Byte code", "Identical", NULL,
         sprintf("Same as GNU R for %s closures of %d packages.", fmt(n_chk, 0), n_chk_pkg))
  else
    tile("#failed", "Byte code", "\u2717 Differs", NULL,
         sprintf("%d of %d packages fail the check.", nrow(chk_failed), n_chk_pkg), "bad"))
```

::: note
The install benchmark is slow, thus it runs only for a new crbcc release.
The compile benchmark is fast, thus it runs in the CI for each commit. The
two benchmarks ran on different machines, at different times, and possibly
with different crbcc versions. Do not compare their times.
:::

```{r failed}
if (nrow(failed) > 0)
  div(class = "alert", id = "failed",
      h3(sprintf("%d failed runs", nrow(failed))),
      p("The statistics do not use these runs."),
      div(class = "scroll", HTML(knitr::kable(
        transmute(failed, suite, package = benchmark, compiler, run, failure = gsub("\\s+", " ", failure)),
        format = "html"))))
```

## How the benchmarks run {#method}

### Install benchmark {#install-method}

Measures
: `R CMD INSTALL` on the CRAN source tarball with `MAKEFLAGS=-j8`.
  `timing-profile.R` gives the times
  **elapsed** (wall time), **native** (`tools:::.shlib_internal`) and
  **bytecode** (`compiler:::tryCmpfun`).

Packages
: `r length(ins_pkgs)`: the `r sum(!ins_pkgs %in% RECOMMENDED)` CRAN
  packages with the most downloads and the
  `r sum(ins_pkgs %in% RECOMMENDED)` recommended packages.

Runs
: For each package, `r ins_runs` runs with GNU R, then `r ins_runs` runs
  with crbcc, one at a time.

Value
: The median of the runs. A total is the sum of the package values.

Machine
: `r machine(ins$meta)`, in the image build.

Software
: `r software(ins$meta)`.

Date
: `r started(ins$meta)`.

### Compile benchmark {#compile-method}

Measures
: The warm time of one `cmpfun()` call for each closure. The closures are
  the namespace functions, S4 methods and R6 methods of a package
  (`crbcc:::package_closures`).

Packages
: The `r n_cl_pkg` packages of the install benchmark.

Runs
: One R process for each package and compiler, with the R JIT off
  (following what `R CMD INSTALL` does). The process does one warm-up
  pass, then `r cl_passes` timed passes. Each timed pass starts with `gc()`
  and uses a new random order.

Value
: The median of the passes for each closure. The speedup of a closure is
  its GNU R time divided by its crbcc time. The headline is the geometric
  mean of the closure speedups.

Excluded
: Closures with a zero time (`r n_zero`) or with times of only one compiler
  (`r n_missing`).

Machine
: `r machine(clo$meta)`, in the CI job `compile`.

Software
: `r software(clo$meta)`.

Date
: `r started(clo$meta)`.

### Byte-code check {#check-method}

Measures
: One compile of each closure with each compiler, in the CI job `compile`.
  A closure fails if the byte codes differ (`crbcc:::identical_strict`) or
  a compiler stops with an error.

Packages
: `r n_chk_pkg`: the base packages without `datasets` and `tcltk`, and the
  packages of the install benchmark.

## Install results {#install-results}

### Total time of `r n_grp[["all"]]` packages

```{r install-bars}
## A bar for each compiler, with a segment for each part of the elapsed
## time. A segment shows its value only if the value fits in it.
widest <- max(all_pk$elapsed_gnur, all_pk$elapsed_crbcc)
install_bar <- function(compiler) {
  v <- sapply(c("native", "bytecode", "rest"), \(m) all_pk[[paste0(m, "_", compiler)]])
  total <- all_pk[[paste0("elapsed_", compiler)]]
  div(div(class = paste("bar-head", compiler), span(span(class = "dot"), NAME[[compiler]]),
          span(fmt(total), "s")),
      div(class = "bar", style = sprintf("width: %.2f%%", 100 * total / widest),
          lapply(names(v), \(m) span(
            class = paste("seg", m),
            style = sprintf("flex-grow: %.4f", max(v[[m]], 0)),
            title = sprintf("%s: %s s", m, fmt(v[[m]])),
            if (v[[m]] / widest >= 0.15) fmt(v[[m]])))))
}
tagList(
  div(class = "bars", install_bar("gnur"), install_bar("crbcc")),
  div(class = "key",
      span(span(class = "sw native"), "native"),
      span(span(class = "sw bytecode"), "bytecode"),
      span(span(class = "sw rest"), "rest: elapsed \u2212 native \u2212 bytecode")))
```

- Byte-code compile: `r fmt(all_pk$bytecode_gnur)` s with GNU R,
  `r fmt(all_pk$bytecode_crbcc)` s with crbcc.
- Elapsed time: `r pct(less[["CRAN"]])` less for the `r n_grp[["CRAN"]]`
  CRAN packages, `r pct(less[["recommended"]])` less for the
  `r n_grp[["recommended"]]` recommended packages.

### The 15 slowest packages

<p class="caption">Elapsed time of <code>R CMD INSTALL</code>. The bar is
the native time. The label gives the change with crbcc.</p>

```{r install-time-plot, fig.height = 5.8, fig.alt = "Elapsed install time of the 15 slowest packages with GNU R and crbcc"}
## A dot for each compiler at the elapsed time of each package, on a bar of
## the native time. The README gets the same figure on a wider canvas, thus
## with smaller text.
install_plot <- function(p) {
  p <- mutate(p, package = factor(package, rev(package)),
              change = round(100 * (elapsed_crbcc / elapsed_gnur - 1)),
              change = paste0(if_else(change > 0, "+", ""), change, "%"))
  dots <- p |>
    select(package, gnur = elapsed_gnur, crbcc = elapsed_crbcc) |>
    pivot_longer(-package, names_to = "compiler")
  ggplot(p, aes(y = package)) +
    geom_col(aes(x = native_gnur), fill = PART[["native"]], width = 0.55) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = elapsed_crbcc, xend = elapsed_gnur), colour = INK3, linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(data = dots, aes(value, fill = compiler), shape = 21, colour = "white",
               size = 3.8, stroke = 1) +
    geom_text(aes(x = pmax(elapsed_gnur, elapsed_crbcc), label = change),
              hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.025 * max(p$elapsed_gnur), size = 4.4, colour = INK2) +
    compiler_fill +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
    labs(x = "elapsed time (s)", y = NULL)
}
top <- install_plot(head(pk, 15))
if (nzchar(params$assets))
  ggsave(file.path(params$assets, "install-time-top15.png"), top,
         width = 8.4, height = 5.8, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
top
```

## Compile results {#compile-results}

### Speedup by closure size

<p class="caption">A point is a closure. The size is the number of AST nodes
(<code>crbcc:::function_size</code>). The line gives the geometric means of
the size classes 1-9, 10-99, and so on.</p>

```{r size-speedup-plot, fig.width = 7.2, fig.height = 4.6, fig.alt = "Compile speedup of each closure against its size"}
x <- cl |> mutate(speedup = gnur / crbcc) |> filter(is.finite(speedup), speedup > 0)
mid <- x |>
  group_by(class) |>
  summarise(size = median(size), speedup = gmean(speedup), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(x, aes(size, speedup)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.15, stroke = 0, colour = INK3) +
  geom_line(data = mid, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = mid, shape = 21, fill = INK, colour = "white", size = 3.2, stroke = 1) +
  geom_text(data = mid, aes(label = times(speedup, 0)), vjust = -1.1, size = 4.4,
            fontface = "bold", colour = INK) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000), labels = \(v) paste0(v, "x")) +
  labs(x = "closure size (AST nodes)", y = "speedup")
```

- Total compile time: `r fmt(cmp[["gnur"]], 2)` s with GNU R,
  `r fmt(cmp[["crbcc"]], 2)` s with crbcc. The ratio of the totals is
  `r times(cmp[["gnur"]] / cmp[["crbcc"]])`, with more weight for large
  closures.

## Data {#data}

<p class="files"><a href="install.csv">install.csv</a><a href="compile.csv">compile.csv</a></p>

The
[`crbcc_bench.py`](https://github.com/PRL-PRG/crbcc/blob/main/inst/benchmarks/crbcc_bench.py)
docstring gives the columns of the raw data.

```{r tables-setup}
## A table that the reader can search and sort. The columns must be numeric,
## because the sort uses the values, not the formatted text. The table has a
## fixed height, thus the line below it gives the row count.
sortable <- function(data, columns, groups) tagList(
  reactable(data, columns = c(list(package = colDef(minWidth = 110, sticky = "left"),
                                   group = colDef(minWidth = 125)), columns),
            columnGroups = groups, searchable = TRUE, pagination = FALSE, height = 480,
            compact = TRUE, highlight = TRUE,
            defaultColDef = colDef(minWidth = 72, headerStyle = list(whiteSpace = "nowrap")),
            theme = reactableTheme(color = INK, borderColor = GRID, highlightColor = "#f6f6f3",
                                   style = list(fontSize = "14px", fontVariantNumeric = "tabular-nums"),
                                   headerStyle = list(color = INK2, fontWeight = 600),
                                   searchInputStyle = list(width = "100%", marginBottom = "8px"))),
  p(class = "caption rows", sprintf("%d packages", nrow(data))))
## The column of one compiler. The CSS puts a dot in its color in the header.
by_compiler <- function(compiler, format) colDef(name = NAME[[compiler]], headerClass = compiler, format = format)
sec <- function(digits) colFormat(digits = digits, separators = TRUE)
```

### Install benchmark

- Times in s, the median of the runs. **native** is the GNU R time,
  because crbcc does not change the native code.
- **reduction**: the part of the GNU R elapsed time that crbcc saves.

```{r install-table}
## Without round(), a value between -0.5% and 0% shows as "-0%". The
## addition of 0 changes a negative zero to zero.
pk |>
  transmute(package, group, elapsed_gnur, elapsed_crbcc, reduction = round(1 - elapsed_crbcc / elapsed_gnur, 2) + 0,
            bytecode_gnur, bytecode_crbcc, native_gnur) |>
  sortable(columns = list(
             elapsed_gnur = by_compiler("gnur", sec(2)), elapsed_crbcc = by_compiler("crbcc", sec(2)),
             reduction = colDef(format = colFormat(percent = TRUE, digits = 0), minWidth = 92),
             bytecode_gnur = by_compiler("gnur", sec(3)), bytecode_crbcc = by_compiler("crbcc", sec(3)),
             native_gnur = colDef(name = "native (s)", format = sec(2), minWidth = 90)),
           groups = list(colGroup("elapsed (s)", c("elapsed_gnur", "elapsed_crbcc", "reduction")),
                         colGroup("bytecode (s)", c("bytecode_gnur", "bytecode_crbcc"))))
```

### Compile benchmark

- **size**: the median closure size, in AST nodes.
- **total**: the median pass time, in ms. A pass time is the sum of its
  closure times.
- **speedup**: the geometric mean of the closure speedups.

```{r compile-table}
cl |>
  group_by(package) |>
  summarise(closures = n(), size = median(size), speedup = gmean(gnur / crbcc)) |>
  inner_join(cl_pk, by = "package") |>
  arrange(desc(gnur)) |>
  transmute(package, group = pkg_group(package), closures, size,
            gnur = 1e3 * gnur, crbcc = 1e3 * crbcc, speedup) |>
  sortable(columns = list(
             closures = colDef(format = sec(0)), size = colDef(format = sec(0)),
             gnur = by_compiler("gnur", sec(1)), crbcc = by_compiler("crbcc", sec(1)),
             speedup = colDef(format = colFormat(digits = 1, suffix = "x"))),
           groups = list(colGroup("total (ms)", c("gnur", "crbcc"))))
```
